definition: A set of circumstances that makes it possible to do something
example: Yes we can, to opportunity and prosperity. Yes we can heal this nation.
speech: New Hampshire Primary Concession / 'Yes We Can' speech

definition: The state of being prosperous
example: Yes we can, to opportunity and prosperity. Yes we can heal this nation.
speech: New Hampshire Primary Concession / 'Yes We Can' speech

definition: A willingness to take bold risks
example: The audacity of hope! In the end, that is God's greatest gift to us, the bedrock of this nation.

definition: A feeling of expectation and desire for a particular thing to happen
example: The audacity of hope! In the end, that is God's greatest gift to us, the bedrock of this nation.

definition: A thing composed of many different elements
example: Our patchwork heritage is a strength, not a weakness.

definition: Property that is or may be inherited; an inheritance
example: Our patchwork heritage is a strength, not a weakness.

definition: The action or fact of joining or being joined
example: The cynics may say that we will never build a more perfect union. But the cynics are wrong.

definition: The events that will necessarily happen to a particular person or thing in the future
example: It was a creed written into the founding documents that declared the destiny of a nation: Yes we can.
speech: New Hampshire Primary Concession / 'Yes We Can' speech

definition: A very brief period of time
example: This is our moment. This is our time.

definition: An alternative route that is shorter than the one usually taken
example: Our journey has never been one of shortcuts or settling for less.
speech: Election Night Victory Speech (Grant Park, Chicago)

definition: Lacking courage or determination
example: Our journey has never been one of shortcuts or settling for less. It has not been the path for the fainthearted.
speech: Election Night Victory Speech (Grant Park, Chicago)

definition: Continuing or long-lasting
example: Obama asks what will prove enduring: 'This is our moment. This is our time.'
source: Their Finest Hour (Churchill, but used in context)

definition: The fundamental principles on which something is based
example: The audacity of hope! In the end, that is God's greatest gift to us, the bedrock of this nation.

definition: A thing given willingly to someone without payment
example: The audacity of hope! In the end, that is God's greatest gift to us, the bedrock of this nation.

definition: Persistence in doing something despite difficulty or delay in achieving success
example: Perseverance means staying the course: America's journey 'has never been one of shortcuts or settling for less.'
speech: Election Night Victory Speech (Grant Park, Chicago)

definition: The available body of facts or information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true or valid
example: Hope is that thing inside us that insists, despite all the evidence to the contrary, that something better awaits us if we have the courage to reach for it.

definition: The ability to do something that frightens one; bravery
example: Hope is that thing inside us that insists, despite all the evidence to the contrary, that something better awaits us if we have the courage to reach for it.

definition: The condition, state, or quality of being free or as free as possible from all flaws or defects
example: Perfection is not the claim — perfecting is: 'This union may never be perfect, but generation after generation has shown that it can always be perfected.'

definition: The nonphysical part of a person which is the seat of emotions and character
example: Obama summons the nation's spirit: 'We are the ones we've been waiting for. We are the change that we seek.'
speech: New Hampshire Primary Concession / 'Yes We Can' speech

definition: A distrust that assumes people act only from selfish motives.
example: Where we are met with cynicism and doubt, and those who tell us that we can't, we will respond with that timeless creed that sums up the spirit of a people: Yes we can.

definition: A real cause for complaint, held by a person or a group.
example: It also means binding our particular grievances to the larger aspirations of all Americans.

definition: Absence of concern, especially toward suffering one could answer.
example: We can no longer afford indifference to suffering outside our borders, nor can we consume the world's resources without regard to effect.

definition: A founding document that grants rights and limits power.
example: Our Founding Fathers drafted a charter to assure the rule of law and the rights of man, a charter expanded by the blood of generations.

definition: A guiding light; a nation or idea that orients others.
example: America stood as a beacon of freedom and opportunity to so many who had come before.

definition: The official ending of a system, especially slavery.
example: The long work of abolition was carried by people who whispered yes we can through the darkest nights.
speech: New Hampshire Primary Concession / 'Yes We Can' speech

definition: Refusal to obey, used as a tool of democratic pressure.
example: What would be needed were Americans willing to do their part — through protests and struggle, through a civil war and civil disobedience, and always at great risk.

definition: To shock or stir people into action.
example: He tried to galvanize a country that had been told, year after year, that nothing could change.
speech: New Hampshire Primary Concession / 'Yes We Can' speech

definition: The condition of many groups sharing one political community; also the largest share short of a majority.
example: A plurality of Americans, not a single tribe, was the country he asked to finish the unfinished work.

definition: A public declaration that something is true and worth holding.
example: Yes we can was an affirmation for people who had been told, often enough, that they could not.
speech: New Hampshire Primary Concession / 'Yes We Can' speech
